sources.title: Hessian Institute for Regional History: Proclamation of Elector Wilhelm I in 1803
sources.note: Indexed original LAGIS scholarly entry via browse/current/25/section/0/pageSize/50/sn/edb. Title acquired1803, Empire ended1806, French occupation and Westphalian incorporation1807, return1813. Canonical idrec returned tool error.

sources.title: Christian Starck: The Electoral Hessian constitution of 1831
sources.note: Direct Kassel University Press 2007 lecture. Printed11 constitutional publication5January1831; pp15to24 agreement, representation and rights; pp26to27 1850 tax conflict, officials/officers resistance and federal intervention. Avoid unsupported democratic universal franchise.

sources.title: Hessian State Centre for Civic Education: Historic boundary stones and territorial change
sources.note: Indexed original official publication, printed4: distinct Kassel/Darmstadt states after1815, Prussian annexation of Electoral Hesse/Nassau/Frankfurt1866. Grand Duchy territorial loss separately. Shared source budgets must include both cards if reused.

sources.title: City of Kassel: Nineteenth-century chronology
sources.note: Direct municipal chronicle. Uses only 1821 coach speed regulation, 1830 bread riot,1832 municipal savings-bank resolution and1872 household water pipes. The latter explicitly after electorate. Constitution ceremonial8January is not substituted for scholarly5Januarypublication.

sources.title: Hessian Institute for Regional History: Educational aims in the 1831 constitution
sources.note: Indexed original via browse/current/302/section/0/pageSize/50/sn/edb. Constitution sections137/138 state educational duty, promised school law, poor elementary-school conditions. Promise is not described as achieved universal provision.

sources.title: GRIMMWELT Kassel: The Children’s and Household Tales
sources.note: Direct museum source: collecting fromKassel1806, first1812edition, revised illustrated smaller1825edition, manuscript corrections and international recognition. Early origin explicitly predates displayed1815interval.

sources.title: GRIMMWELT Kassel: Who told the tales
sources.note: Direct/indexed museum scholarship: largely young educated women, Huguenot/European connections, Viehmann tailor’s wife not wandering peasant informant; versions revised.

sources.title: Brothers Grimm: Little Red Riding Hood, second edition, 1819
sources.note: Direct/indexed transcription of original1819G.Reimer Berlin edition, volume1 printed138. Sample exact Ei Großmutter, was hast du für große Ohren! Modern transcription linked to page images. UniversityKassel facsimile links failed web access; do not claim original image visually inspected.

sources.title: City of Kassel: Historical anniversaries for 2023
sources.note: Direct/indexed municipal history:29July1848Henschel first locomotive delivered to Friedrich-Wilhelm-Nordbahn, named Drache; rail opening18August1848.

sources.title: City of Kassel: Historical anniversaries for 2025
sources.note: Direct/indexed municipal history: gasworks outsideHolländischesTor1850 suppliesstreetlighting. No claim gas reached everyhouse.

sources.title: Hessian state government: The nineteenth-century political map
sources.note: Direct official historical overview: elevation and Confederation of the Rhine in 1806, territorial changes, constitution of 17 December 1820. Electoral Hesse dates elsewhere in this source conflict with detailed scholarship and are not used.

sources.title: Darmstadt regional government: The Kollegiengebäude and Hessian administration
sources.note: Direct government PDF. Section 2.1, PDF index 13, printed pages 26 to 27: deposition in 1918, Volksstaat, constitution in December 1919. Provinces Starkenburg, Oberhessen and Rheinhessen.

sources.title: Leibniz Institute of European History: Rheinhessen province
sources.note: Indexed original academic historical-geography entry; direct tool request failed. Province formed in 1816 after Congress of Vienna allocation; Napoleonic civil law retained, in contrast with other two provinces.

sources.title: Georg Büchner and Friedrich Ludwig Weidig: The Hessian Courier, July 1834
sources.note: Direct proofread transcription of original July 1834 pamphlet, page 1: Friede den Hütten! Krieg den Pallästen! Double l in original Pallästen retained. Publicly identified as transcription. Introductory precautions and account of taxation are pamphlet rhetoric, not accepted neutral statistics.

sources.title: Hessian State Centre for Civic Education: Georg Büchner and his family
sources.note: Direct PDF text, printed pages 6 to 7 constitution and monarchical limits; printed 14, PDF index 15, Landbote title-page reproduction and flight in March 1835. Screenshot request did not deliver a usable image; exact writing verified against primary transcription instead.

sources.title: Liebig Museum: History of the laboratory
sources.note: Direct museum history. Appointment 1824, former guardhouse, five ground-floor rooms, family upstairs, initial 12 students taught in private room.

sources.title: Justus Liebig University: Its namesake and his chemistry
sources.note: Direct university source: organic analysis improved with five-bulb kali apparatus removing carbon dioxide; 1824 appointment. Avoids sole-inventor or immediate universal adoption claims.

sources.title: Opel historical collection: The company’s beginnings in 1862
sources.note: Direct company historical release dated 29 August 2022. Family-house workshop 1862, disused cowshed 1863, new steam-powered factory and 40 workers in 1868; Sophie managed bookkeeping. Marketing claims not repeated.

sources.title: Darmstadt City Encyclopedia: Alice women’s associations
sources.note: Direct municipal scholarly encyclopedia, Agnes Schmidt. June 1867 nursing association, non-confessional training of four to five months paid by association; vocational courses and host families for out-of-town students, teacher courses in 1875.

sources.title: Darmstadt City Encyclopedia: Women’s movement
sources.note: Direct/indexed municipal article: Luise Büchner 1855 educational demands, 1872 meeting and demands for public-service jobs and kindergarten provision. Demands are not treated as immediately realized.

sources.title: Darmstadt City Encyclopedia: Water supply
sources.note: Direct municipal article: 1871 planning, polluted inadequate supply, waterworks opened 1 December 1880, six wells, steam pumps and elevated reservoir. Post-map chronology explicit.

sources.title: Darmstadt City Encyclopedia: Sewage treatment
sources.note: Direct municipal article by Peter Engels: cesspits and fertilizer collection, drains and refuse, 1881 main collectors, March 1883 network then one year later 937 buildings/187 water closets. Thus toilet counts are 1884, not 1882.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Map1815to1878polygon bbox8.1703,50.0769to9.9271,51.5979 fitsHesse-Kassel corridor approximately but falsely persists beyond1866. Publicoverview/end warnexplicitly. DistinctfromDarmstadtGrandDuchy. No geometrychanges.

Imported 1815 to 1878 record has two separate northern and southern components. Distinct from Electoral Hesse. Rheinhessen acquisition belongs to 1816 and historical monarchy ends in 1918, both made public. Later water and toilet evidence explicitly extends beyond imported cutoff without claiming the state ended in 1878.
